name: Gulf / US–Iran war
value: IRGC claims US drone downed 14 Nov; US blockade
summary: Iran says it downed a US drone over Qeshm on 14 Nov as tanker mine claims continue; US blockade of Iranian ports holds
state: The IRGC said it shot down a US MQ-1 drone over Qeshm Island on 14 Nov and Iran's navy said two tankers caught fire after hitting mines that day; CENTCOM had rejected an IRGC claim to have destroyed a US radar in Bahrain, saying it downed two Iranian drones (ANI via The Tribune). On 11 Nov Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Hormuz would stay shut until US conditions are met, while President Trump said new attacks were not needed (Al Jazeera). The US blockade of Iranian ports continues (The New Arab, 14 Nov).
for_you: Travellers to Iran and the Gulf states should check FCDO travel advice before and during travel. Energy and shipping markets remain exposed to further attacks on tankers and Gulf infrastructure.
rubric_hit: Alert: active state-on-state hostilities and continuing attacks on Gulf shipping (claims 13–14 Nov)

sources.title: The Tribune (ANI) — Iran claims 17th US MQ-1 drone destroyed; 2 tankers catch fire in Strait of Hormuz
Al Jazeera — Iran denies talks with US, says Hormuz will stay shut until demands are met
The New Arab — UN official urges Iran, US to let fertilisers through Hormuz

why: Direct hostilities between Iran and the US or Israel threaten Gulf energy infrastructure, the Strait of Hormuz and the wider region.
drivers: Strikes and retaliation, attacks on shipping and Gulf states, mediation and ceasefire talks, US force posture.

rubric.alert: Active strikes between states, attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure or shipping, or the Strait of Hormuz substantially closed.
rubric.watch: A ceasefire or stalemate with sporadic strikes, or credible threats of renewed strikes.
rubric.normal: No direct state-on-state hostilities; diplomacy active.
